newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity prices hit new highs in up trend.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity prices hit new highs in up trend.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures hit new contract highs Friday in an upward trend driven by cooler weather, strong natural gas prices and limited spot power supplies in the U.S. Northwest, industry sources said.
Although NYMEX California-Oregon Border (COB) hit an new spot contract high Friday, some traders said the market could sell off later in the day with some players holding stops at higher levels.
"People are still trying to figure out exactly what is taking place here, but we could see a selloff yet today," said one New York-based futures broker.
Bonneville Power Administration said Friday it was not offering surplus power for sale Saturday and Sunday and would offer limited sales of 300 megawatts on Monday during peak hours.
Power futures prices may also be feeling the impact of some consolidation ahead of Monday's November contract expiry, the sources said.
As of 1230 EDT, November COB was trading up 90 cents at $21.15 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new all-time COB futures high of $21.75 per MWh.
December COB was trading up 15 cents at $20.80, while remaining COB deferreds were steady to up to 45 cents higher.
November Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 22 cents at $19.15 after hitting a new contract high of $20.25 per MWh, while Decmeber was 20 cents higher at $19.00 after trade as high as $19.50 per MWh.
January and February PV were trading down five to 10 cents, while remaining PV months were steady to 35 cents higher.
NYMEX said that as of 1205 EDT a total of 68 COB contracts and 137 PV contracts had traded.
COB open interest for Oct 24 rose 103 to 3,808 while PV open interest rose 70 to 1,858, NYMEX said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
